issues.t: Plastic cooling parts crack and the engine overheats
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front of the car, a sweet smell after driving, the low-coolant light, or the temperature needle climbing above the middle.
issues.why: The radiator end tanks, expansion tank, thermostat housing and hoses on these roadsters are plastic. After years of heating and cooling they turn brittle and crack, often with little warning.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge climbs, because overheating these inline-6 engines can warp the head. If the car is past 80,000 miles or 15 years old, many owners replace the radiator, tank, thermostat, water pump and hoses together as a planned refresh.

issues.t: Electric water pump fails without warning
issues.sym: A coolant temperature warning on the dash, the engine dropping into reduced power, or the car overheating suddenly, sometimes right after a cold start.
issues.why: Starting with the 2006 models, these engines use an electric water pump instead of a belt-driven one. Its motor and circuit board wear out, usually somewhere between 60,000 and 100,000 miles, and it often quits all at once.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if a temperature warning appears. If the pump has never been changed and the car is near 70,000 miles, replacing the pump and thermostat ahead of time is common practice.

issues.t: Rod bearing wear on the M Roadster and M Coupe engine
issues.sym: Often nothing at first. Later a knocking from the bottom of the engine, low oil pressure warnings, or metal flakes in the oil.
issues.why: The high-revving 3.2L S54 engine is known for wearing its connecting rod bearings early, especially when oil changes were stretched out. A spun bearing can destroy the engine.
issues.next: Change the oil every 5,000 miles or so and ask whether the rod bearings have been replaced. Many specialists replace them as preventive maintenance to avoid needing a new engine.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or shifts harshly
issues.sym: Slow or harsh shifts, the engine revving between gears, slipping, or the car not wanting to move in drive.
issues.why: The automatic transmission in early Z4s has a reputation for failing, sometimes at fairly low mileage. Old fluid that was never changed makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked and the transmission scanned for codes. If it is slipping, avoid hard driving and get a transmission specialist's opinion before it fails completely.

issues.t: Electric power steering feels sticky or notchy
issues.sym: The steering feels sticky near center, needs uneven effort, or the car seems to wander or drift on the highway.
issues.why: Non-M Z4s of this generation use an electric motor on the steering column for power assist. The motor and the steering column joints can wear and bind. Later cars from about 2006 are less affected.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have a BMW specialist check the steering column motor and joints. Lubricating or adjusting the column sometimes helps; a worn motor or rack needs replacement.

issues.t: Convertible top pump fails or gets flooded
issues.sym: The soft top stops partway, won't open or close, moves slowly, or you hear the pump run with nothing happening. Hydraulic fluid may be found in the trunk.
issues.why: The top's hydraulic pump sits low in the trunk. Blocked drains or leaking trunk seals let water collect and corrode the motor. The lift cylinders and lock motor also wear with age.
issues.next: Clear the top and trunk drains and check for water in the trunk. Have the pump, cylinders and wiring tested before replacing the whole system; used parts are an option.

issues.t: VANOS valve timing seals wear out
issues.sym: Rough idle, a rattle when starting cold, weak pull at low speed and slightly worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The VANOS system adjusts valve timing using oil pressure. Its rubber seals harden and leak with age, so the system can no longer hold the right timing.
issues.next: Have the VANOS unit checked. New seals usually fix it, and this is a well-known repair at independent BMW shops.

issues.t: VANOS failure on the M Roadster and M Coupe
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, rough running, loss of power at high revs, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The S54 engine's individual VANOS system is more complex than the regular engines'. Its seals, solenoids and pump parts wear, and loose parts can damage the engine if ignored.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new rattle. Have a specialist inspect the VANOS and rebuild it; doing it early avoids much bigger repairs.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak oil
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, light smoke from under the hood, oil on the engine, or oil in the spark plug wells.
issues.why: The rubber gaskets on the valve cover and oil filter housing harden with heat and age, letting oil seep onto the hot exhaust.
issues.next: Fix it soon. Oil dripping on the exhaust can start a fire, and oil in the plug wells causes misfires. Check the drive belt too, since leaking oil can ruin it.

issues.t: Crankcase vent valve clogs and the engine burns oil
issues.sym: Blue smoke at startup, using more oil than before, a rough idle, or a whistle from the engine.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (CCV) valve and its hoses clog and split with age. That raises pressure inside the engine and pulls oil into the intake.
issues.next: Have the CCV system checked; replacing it is a common fix. Keep an eye on the oil level until it's done.

issues.t: Valvetronic eccentric shaft sensor fails
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rough or hunting idle, poor throttle response, or the engine going into reduced power mode.
issues.why: This engine controls air flow with a variable valve lift system called Valvetronic. The sensor that reads its position wears out, usually after 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A failed sensor is replaced; a leaking sensor gasket can cause similar faults.

issues.t: Power window regulator breaks
issues.sym: The window drops into the door, moves crooked, stops working, or makes a grinding or clicking noise.
issues.why: The regulator's plastic clips and guides that hold the glass are weak and break with age.
issues.next: Avoid using the window until it's fixed and cover it if it's stuck open. A new regulator fixes it.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm bushings wear out
issues.sym: The rear of the car feels loose or wanders over bumps, clunks from the back, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings where the rear trailing arms attach to the body crack and sag with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected. New bushings are a common repair and an alignment afterward is a good idea.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear, vague steering or shake when braking
issues.sym: Vague or wandering steering, clunks over bumps, a steering wheel shake when braking from highway speed, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms crack and collapse over time.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Replacing the bushings or arms and getting an alignment usually fixes it.

issues.t: Rear subframe and differential mounts crack
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear when accelerating or letting off, a loose feel from the back, or rust and cracks around the rear axle mounts.
issues.why: The body around the rear subframe and differential mounting points can rust and crack, especially on cars driven hard or kept in salty areas.
issues.next: Have the rear subframe and differential mounts inspected on a lift. Cracks need welding by a body shop before they get worse.

issues.t: Water leaks into the trunk
issues.sym: Damp carpet or standing water in the trunk, a musty smell, or electrical faults from parts kept in the trunk.
issues.why: Trunk seals and the seal under the third brake light shrink with age. Blocked roof drains add to the problem.
issues.next: Find and replace the leaking seal and clear the drains. Dry the trunk fully, since water there can ruin the top pump and the battery area.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor on the 1.9L
issues.sym: A check engine light, worse fuel economy, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The oxygen sensors on the four-cylinder Z3 are the most common reason for an engine warning light. A noisy timing chain is also reported on these engines.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If an oxygen sensor is to blame, replacing it is a simple job.

issues.t: Cruise control cable can hold the throttle open (recall)
issues.sym: The engine doesn't slow down when you lift off the gas, especially after using cruise control.
issues.why: A cruise control or throttle cable problem could keep the throttle partly open.
issues.next: If the car keeps accelerating, shift to neutral and brake. Check your VIN with BMW to confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Fuel pump vapor lock can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or loses power, mostly in hot weather, and may be hard to restart.
issues.why: On some early Z4s the electric fuel pump can vapor lock when hot, cutting fuel to the engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Make sure the recall was done; a BMW dealer can check by VIN.

issues.t: Crankcase vent heater can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. In some cases a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even with the car parked.
issues.why: A heater in the crankcase vent valve can short out and overheat, melting nearby parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls and have it fixed right away. Park outside until the recall work is done.

issues.t: Battery cable connector can cut power and stall the car (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses electrical power, stalls, or won't start.
issues.why: The connection at the battery cable can lose contact, cutting power to the whole car.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a BMW dealer check your VIN for this recall and complete the repair.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump fails on the sDrive35i
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, stalling, stumbling under acceleration, and a check engine light or reduced power.
issues.why: The twin-turbo N54 engine's high-pressure fuel pump was a known failure point. Many were replaced with improved pumps early in the car's life.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure codes read. Ask whether the pump was updated; BMW extended warranty coverage on these pumps for many cars.

issues.t: Leaking or misfiring fuel injectors on the sDrive35i
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, hard starting when warm, a fuel smell, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The direct-injection injectors on the N54 engine can leak or fail. A leaking injector can wash oil off the cylinder walls.
issues.next: Get misfire codes diagnosed promptly. Injectors are usually replaced with the latest version, sometimes as a full set.

issues.t: Timing chain guides wear on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: A whine or rattle from the engine, especially on cold starts, then a check engine light. In the worst case the chain breaks and the engine is ruined.
issues.why: The plastic guides for the timing chain on the N20 engine can wear and break, letting the chain slap or jump.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new whine or rattle. Have the chain and guides inspected and replaced with updated parts.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can fail and the pedal gets hard (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly needs much more force to stop the car.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can lose lubrication and fail.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the recall done right away if it is still open. The brakes still work, but you must push much harder.

issues.t: Water pump connector can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Possibly a burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: An electrical short at the electric coolant pump can overheat and create a fire risk.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for this recall and get it fixed. Park outside and away from buildings until it is done.

issues.t: Retractable hardtop stops working or opens partway
issues.sym: The folding hardtop won't open or close, stops partway, takes much longer than about 20 seconds, or shows a roof error. Rattles from the roof over bumps are also common.
issues.why: Sensors and settings that tell the roof where it is in its cycle can fail or go out of adjustment. Moisture near the roof mechanism and battery makes it worse.
issues.next: Test the roof several times before buying. Have a BMW specialist read the roof module codes before replacing parts, since a sensor is often the cause.

issues.t: Bent or cracked wheels on low-profile run-flat tires
issues.sym: A vibration at speed, a tire that slowly loses air, or a visible bend on the inside of the rim.
issues.why: The larger optional wheels use stiff, low-profile run-flat tires. Potholes and curbs can bend or crack the rims, and the damage is easy to miss.
issues.next: Check tire pressures often. If one keeps losing air, have the wheel checked for cracks or bends on a balancer.

issues.t: Rearview camera image can go missing (recall)
issues.sym: No picture on the screen when reversing, or the camera view can be turned off in the settings.
issues.why: A software problem can leave the backup camera display blank.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer update the software. Use your mirrors and look behind you until it is done.

issues.t: Brake assist can drop out right after starting (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal right after starting the engine.
issues.why: Engine software could cut the brake power assist during engine start. The brakes still work but need more force.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have a BMW dealer install the software update.

issues.t: Starter or starter relay can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Possibly a burning smell, or a starter that clicks or struggles.
issues.why: Corrosion in the starter relay or wear inside the starter motor can make it overheat and short out.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls. Park outside and away from buildings until the dealer replaces the starter.

issues.t: Oil filter housing gasket leaks on the M40i
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine, oil on the belt area, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The gasket between the oil filter housing and the engine block on the 3.0L turbo seeps oil. It is the most common oil leak on this engine.
issues.next: Have it fixed before oil soaks the drive belt and other rubber parts. The repair needs some parts removed but is routine for BMW shops.

issues.t: Coolant expansion tank and hoses seep coolant
issues.sym: A low-coolant warning, a sweet smell under the hood, or white crust on the coolant tank or hoses.
issues.why: The plastic expansion tank and coolant hoses can develop small leaks over time.
issues.next: Top up with the correct BMW coolant and have the system pressure-tested. Replace the tank or hose that is leaking.

issues.t: Electric water pump or thermostat fails on the M40i
issues.sym: Engine temperature warnings, overheating, or the car limiting power.
issues.why: The electric water pump and thermostat housing are known weak points on BMW's 3.0L turbo six.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. Have the pump and thermostat tested; many owners replace them ahead of time at higher mileage.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear and clunk
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, steering that feels less precise, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The sporty suspension tuning puts a lot of stress on the front lower control arm bushings.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked for play. New control arms and an alignment fix it.
